context: Yumiko reminisces about old festivals with Naoko at the ramen shop.
purpose: Two older women sharing nostalgic festival memories.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 昔の祭り、賑やかだったわね。
lines.en: Those old festivals were so lively, weren't they.
lines.style: Warm exhale on the opening. Soft, nostalgic tone. Gentle pace. Eyes slightly distant, looking back into memory. The comfort of shared history.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.jp: ほんま、屋台、いっぱいやった。
lines.en: They really were. So many food stalls everywhere.
lines.style: Bright affirmation with Kansai lilt. Energetic but not loud — animated recollection. A quick laugh underneath. Leaning in with the memory, engaged and alive.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.en: And we all danced the bon dance together.
lines.style: Soft, almost singing quality to the delivery. Unhurried pace. The voice settles into the memory gently, like a blanket. Slight warmth on 「皆で」.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: I still remember it, you know.
lines.style: Quiet conviction underneath the softness. A touch of Kansai warmth on the end. Not wistful — present with the memory. Settling into it like it's happening again.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.en: We really were so young then.
lines.style: Gentle sigh on the opening. Slow, reflective pace. A slight catch — not sad, but aware of time passing. Voice trails off softly on the final word.

lines.speaker: naoko_aunt
lines.en: Well I still feel young in my head!
lines.style: Bright, defiant laugh. Kansai accent stronger here. Quick tempo, playful edge. A little pride underneath — refusal to age gracefully, chosen cheerfulness. Leans back with the joke.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.en: That's the spirit — keep that up.
lines.style: Warm, approving chuckle. Soft but genuine. A small light tap on 「意気」. The tone of someone who loves what they just heard. Gentle affection settling in the voice.
